To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson): Aria 3 recalibration, sensor and battery

Last month I told Dana in the "Anyone used Harbor Point" thread that I'd write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial, so here it is, following Ellen's pinned list.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3
Shop: Harbor Point Steno Service, off York Road in Towson. It's a two-person shop, and parking in back is free.
Dropped off: Monday, October 19
Picked up: Tuesday, October 27
Quoted: $285 and 10 business days
Paid: $310 total. The extra $25 was a battery I approved partway through.
Loaner: Yes, an Aria 2
Who paid: I did. I buy all my own equipment, and there was no reimbursement from the court.

The work
I asked for a full recalibration, a number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and a firmware update. The invoice shows the number bar depression sensor was replaced, the firmware went from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and the internal battery was replaced. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The machine was ready in six business days against the ten quoted. It also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made, which I have never gotten from any shop before.

The battery
On October 22 Gloria Ruark emailed to say the battery was holding about 60% of rated capacity. Replacing it would be $25 in parts and labor, and she said she would not go ahead without my approval. I said yes. It's a small thing, but being asked first matters to me, and $310 is fair for everything that was done.

How it held up
My first full day back with the machine was expert testimony from an engineer who talks almost entirely in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke, and it has been clean through the rest of the trial since.

The loaner
The Aria 2 they lent me had a tilt arm that would not hold its position. It slipped in the middle of an afternoon deposition and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I emailed Gloria and she wrote back that they would repair it. It's minor, but if you will be writing on the loaner for a full day, test the arm before you leave the shop.

The weak spot: the phone
Their phone line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that's it. I called on Wednesday, October 21 to ask how things were going. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed me the next day, so I wasn't left hanging, but if you are in court most weekdays or work a Monday docket, you will not reach them by phone in any practical way. Everything that mattered on my job came through email: the work order, the battery question, and the pickup notice with the invoice. Plan on email.

Bottom line
Dana, since you asked: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. The work was careful, the pricing matched the quote apart from a repair I approved, and the communication was honest, even if it wasn't by phone. Drop the machine off knowing you'll be dealing with Gloria by email, take the loaner and check its tilt arm, and expect it back in about a week. I would go back, and I would also keep their email address handy and not count on the phone.

Maureen
